summary: Ozark National Forest tower in Franklin County; a 1971 survey describes a steel tower about 75 ft high with an orange cabin. Current status unknown.

facts.design: four-legged steel skeleton tower with a cabin on top, painted orange
facts.status_note: The newest description found is from 1971; no current source confirms that the tower still stands.

visit.trail_note: 1971 survey directions: north on State Highway 23 past the Cass work center, then a graded road east, a side road with a sign for the tower, and a bladed road south for 0.15 mile to the station.

events.note: National Geodetic Survey station description: four-legged steel tower about 75 feet high, with a cabin painted orange.

notes_for_editor: Single source: a lookout-history website that reproduces a 1971 National Geodetic Survey station description. Nothing found on build date, staffing, fires, fate or current condition. Brief status (unknown) kept as unknown. Brief values are supported: height 22.9 m matches 'about 75 feet'; agency and Franklin County match the description. No corrections proposed. Searches: two web searches, then the cached NHLR Arkansas list (it does not include Fly Gap) and the Encyclopedia of Arkansas lookout entry (general, nothing on this tower). Topo-directory pages returned 403 and were not used. Access directions are 1971 survey directions and were not checked against current roads.
